package_info.why_malicious: The package itself is not malicious, but running it on Java 7 exposes users to unpatched vulnerabilities due to unsupported dependencies. The risk is that future security fixes may require Java 8, and users remaining on Java 7 will be left with exploitable vulnerabilities.

attack_chain.action: A vulnerability is disclosed in an open source dependency used by Nexus Repository Manager 2.x.
attack_chain.leads_to: Potential exploitation if the vulnerability is not patched.

attack_chain.action: A fix for the vulnerability is released, but it requires upgrading to Java 8 due to dependency requirements.
attack_chain.leads_to: Users on Java 7 cannot apply the fix.

attack_chain.action: Users who have not upgraded to Java 8 remain exposed to the publicized, exploitable vulnerability.
attack_chain.leads_to: Potential compromise of the repository manager and its data.

behavioral_signatures: Running Nexus Repository Manager 2.x on Java 7
Use of outdated or unsupported Java runtime environments
Inability to apply security patches due to Java version constraints
network_indicators: No direct network indicators; risk is from unpatched vulnerabilities being exploited
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for instances of Nexus Repository Manager 2.x running on Java 7. Check the Java runtime version in use by the application. Flag any deployments that cannot apply the latest security patches due to Java version incompatibility. Proactively alert administrators to upgrade to Java 8 to ensure continued security support.
